jobs.title: RN Case Manager - Hospice
jobs.description:
**Registered Nurse Case Manager (RNCM)**
========================================

**Horizon Hospice of Colorado**  

**Full\-Time \| 0\.8 FTE with Growth to 1\.0 FTE**

**Position Summary**
--------------------


Horizon Hospice of Colorado is seeking an experienced **Registered Nurse Case Manager (RNCM)** to provide compassionate, high\-quality hospice care to patients and families throughout the Denver Metro area.


The RN Case Manager serves as the primary clinical coordinator for an assigned group of hospice patients and works closely with the interdisciplinary team to ensure care is individualized, well\-coordinated, and focused on comfort, dignity, and quality of life.


This position includes direct patient care, symptom management, family education, care coordination, interdisciplinary collaboration, and clinical documentation.

**ScheduleFTE Structure**
-------------------------


This is a **full\-time position initially structured at 0\.8 FTE (32 hours per week)**, with the opportunity to increase to **1\.0 FTE (40 hours per week)** as hospice census and caseload grow.


RN Case Manager caseload expectations are based on patient census, acuity, geography, and individual care needs.

**Typical full RNCM caseload: 12\-15 patients**, depending on patient complexity and travel requirements.


Our goal is to increase this position to 1\.0 FTE as patient census supports a full RN Case Manager caseload.

**Essential Responsibilities**
------------------------------

### **Patient CareClinical Management**

* Complete comprehensive nursing assessments and ongoing reassessments of patient needs.
* Develop, implement, and update individualized hospice plans of care in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team.
* Provide skilled nursing visits in private homes, assisted living communities, skilled nursing facilities, and other care settings.
* Assess and manage pain, symptoms, functional decline, and changes in patient condition.
* Administer medications, treatments, and interventions as ordered.
* Educate patients and caregivers regarding medications, symptom management, disease progression, end\-of\-life changes, and when to contact hospice.
* Provide support and clinical guidance during changes in condition and symptom crises.
* Perform pronouncement of death and post\-mortem care when appropriate and in accordance with hospice policy.
* Complete timely and accurate documentation in the electronic medical record.

### **Care CoordinationInterdisciplinary Collaboration**

* Serve as the primary clinical coordinator for assigned hospice patients.
* Collaborate with physicians, social workers, chaplains, hospice aides, therapists, volunteers, and other members of the interdisciplinary team.
* Participate in interdisciplinary team (IDT) meetings and contribute meaningfully to patient care planning and review.
* Communicate changes in patient status, goals, symptoms, and care needs to appropriate team members.
* Coordinate medications, durable medical equipment, supplies, and additional services needed to support the patient plan of care.
* Facilitate continuity of care when patients transition between care settings.

### **PatientFamily Support**

* Provide education, guidance, and emotional support to patients and families throughout the hospice journey.
* Help patients and caregivers understand hospice services, the plan of care, and what to expect as illness progresses.
* Support families during the active dying process and end\-of\-life transition.
* Promote patient dignity, comfort, autonomy, and quality of life.

### **ComplianceDocumentation**

* Maintain clinical documentation consistent with hospice regulatory requirements, organizational policies, and standards of care.
* Complete assessments, care plans, visit documentation, orders, and care coordination notes accurately and within required timeframes.
* Support compliance with Medicare Hospice Conditions of Participation and applicable state requirements.
* Participate in quality improvement initiatives, chart audits, education, and clinical competency activities as requested.
* Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with HIPAA requirements.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Current, unrestricted **Registered Nurse (RN) license in the State of Colorado**.
* **Minimum of one year of hospice nursing experience required.**
* Strong clinical assessment, critical thinking, and symptom\-management skills.
* Experience caring for patients with advanced illness and end\-of\-life needs.
* Ability to work independently in community\-based settings while collaborating effectively with an interdisciplinary team.
* Strong communication, organization, documentation, and time\-management skills.
* Comfortable providing patient and caregiver education in emotionally sensitive situations.
* Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and ability to travel throughout the service area.
* Current CPR certification.

**Compensation**
----------------

**$43\-$48 per hour equivalent, paid as salary based on established FTE, experience, and qualifications.**

* **0\.8 FTE / 32 hours per week:** approximately **$71,552\-$79,872 annually**
* **1\.0 FTE / 40 hours per week:** approximately **$89,440\-$99,840 annually**


Mileage reimbursement is provided for eligible business travel.

-------------------------------------


Horizon Hospice of Colorado is committed to providing compassionate, individualized hospice care centered on the needs and goals of each patient and family.

jobs.description:
Description:  

We are an amazing organization and we’re looking to grow our workforce in some critical areas. If you’re looking for a position where you can use your skills to make a difference in the lives of others, look no further! We are truly a rewarding place to work. It’s an organization where ability and compassion combine to create unmatched service. We value our employees and have built an organization that embraces diversity, supports team members and encourages growth. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.


More About Us:


We provide Senior Living and Assisted Living apartment homes for adults 62 years of age and older (and people with qualifying mobility impairment disabilities). Our residences and main office are in the beautiful Cherry Creek neighborhood, convenient to the Cherry Creek Mall, restaurants, movie theater, shops, tennis courts and walking paths. Our team members provide quality care, services and support to our residents and the broader community. In turn, it is our philosophy to provide a rich compensation and benefits package with flexibility, affordability and ease of use in mind.


Through our commitment to hiring well\-qualified candidates and maintaining a safe working environment we conduct preemployment screening on all prospective employees.


Our nonprofit organization is currently seeking a **Full\-Time Assisted Living Care Coordinator** to join our team! A compassionate, skilled Care Coordinator to support the behavioral health and emotional well\-being of older adults. This role connects residents with needed resources and support, provides behavioral health interventions, and offers crisis support when appropriate. If you’re looking for work where you can make a difference and be a part of a great team this may be the position for you.


The ideal candidate has experience supporting older adults and individuals with behavioral health needs, including depression, anxiety, grief and loss, adjustment challenges, cognitive changes, behavioral concerns, and other psychosocial issues. The Care Coordinator serves as an essential behavioral health resource within our senior living community, promoting dignity, connection, emotional well\-being, and quality of life for residents and their families.

**Schedule:** Monday\-Friday, 40 hours per week, between 7:30am and 5:30pm

* Monitor resident well\-being, including changes in mood, behavior, functioning, hospitalizations, temporary placements, and community returns, implementing appropriate interventions and follow\-up as needed.
* Coordinate and facilitate resident care plan reviews in collaboration with the Wellness Coordinator, ensuring care plans accurately reflect changing resident needs and service requirements.
* Collaborate with residents, families, caregivers, healthcare providers, case managers, staff, and interdisciplinary teams to address behavioral health, psychosocial, medical, and housing\-related concerns.
* Assist residents and families with transitions related to housing, healthcare needs, cognitive decline, loss of independence, end\-of\-life concerns, and community resource navigation, including placement when residents no longer meet assisted living eligibility requirements.
* Coordinate referrals to behavioral health, psychiatric, counseling, community support, housing, and other service providers as appropriate.
* Assist residents with applications and access to benefits and services, including Medicaid, SSDI, AND, HCBS, PTC, long\-term care programs, and other available resources when needed.
* Manage and coordinate Medicaid renewals and eligibility\-related issues, working directly with government and community agencies to ensure continuity of benefits and services.
* Serve as a liaison and advocate regarding insurance benefits, Medicaid programs, long\-term care options, and other resident support services.
* Coordinate with Health \& Wellness staff regarding resident appointments, activity participation, hospitalizations, temporary placements, and other care coordination needs.
* Provide consultation, education, training, and support to staff and families regarding mental health, behavioral symptoms, communication strategies, aging\-related psychosocial issues, bereavement, and resident support needs.
* Facilitate therapeutic, educational, support, and engagement groups and programs that promote social connection, community involvement, and resident well\-being.
* Assist residents with practical support needs, including correspondence, reading mail, telephone communication, and other activities that promote independence and self\-advocacy.

jobs.title: Program Supervisor | First Episode of Psychosis
jobs.description:
As our Program Supervisor you will be responsible for the coordination and management of the assigned Mental Health Partners (MHP) program(s), providing leadership to staff and serving as the primary point of communication.


**Job Summary:**



You will oversee the daily operations of the assigned program(s) serving as the primary point of communication, oversight and decision\-making regarding program needs, requirements, and development. You will conduct the hiring, training and supervision of your team. You will be a working supervisor who may also provide direct service to clients.


**Specialized Duties:**


*ASCENT team:*


* You will provide supervision of CFHW ASCENT team (First Episode Psychosis program) which provides community\-based services to clients 15\-29 years old experiencing an onset of psychotic disorders at our Sherman facility.
* Work alongside Manager and Supervisor of Longmont Behavioral Health Home and ACT Team. This includes assuring facility site issues are addressed to appropriate CFHW department, coordination of coverage of client services, and other duties required to maintain Sherman site as a safe and welcoming environment.
* You will provide supervision of ASCENT clinicians, to promote adherence and fidelity to ASCENT model by conducting 3x weekly staffing, preparing planning notes and progress notes for the weekly staffing, and developing a specific plan and goals for the group to match the supervision model of ASCENT.
* You will promote quality improvement of the ASCENT model by supporting ASCENT staff with adherence and competence.
* Utilize specific supervision interventions, informal improvement plans and formalized improvement plans, such as quarterly reports to monitor fidelity and performance, and quality assurance through the BHA computer database.
* You will collaborate with other partner agencies to support sustainability of the ASCENT model.
* Provide clinical intervention to clients and support staff in crisis situations.
* Manage and carry a client caseload for supporting ASCENT program.


**Supervisory Duties:**


* You will demonstrate awareness, support, and appreciation for cultural and diversity issues.
* Work as part of a collaborative team of individuals to provide a high level of intensive services to clients.
* Lead regular staff meetings to promote teamwork, sustain an aligned and energized work force, promote communication, and provide team direction.
* May recommend and manage program budget ensuring for cost\-effective utilization of CFHW resources.

  


**What We Need:**


* Master’s degree in psychology, Social Work, Counseling, or related field \+ 1\- or 2\-year internship
* Three (3\+) years’ relevant experience including at least 1 years’ relevant supervisory experience.
* Licensed PhD or PsyD, Licensed Clinical Social worker (LCSW), Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC), or Licensed Marriage/Family Therapist (LMFT) required.
* Experience working with mentally ill population in outpatient and community\-based settings.

  


**What’s In It For You:**


* + Comprehensive benefits:
	+ Medical, Dental \& Vision options
	+ Medical and Dependent Care FSA/HSA
	+ Company paid life insurance
	+ Long term disability insurance
	+ Accident/hospital plans
	+ 403(b) Retirement Plan with employer contributions
	+ CFWH offers vacation time, sick hours, and personal holiday hours.
	+ A collaborative team environment.
	+ Open communication with leadership and mission\-focused engagement
	+ Training and growth opportunities with a supportive team invested in your success

Compensation: $63,757\.82 \- $$102,021\.09, annualized The posted range represents the full salary range for this position. Starting pay is based on factors such as directly related experience, education, licensure and/or certification, and internal equity.



CFHW is committed to an inclusive, age\-neutral hiring process. In compliance with the Colorado Job Application Fairness Act (JAFA), we do not ask applicants to disclose their age, date of birth, or dates of attendance/graduation from an educational institution. Please focus your application on your relevant skills, qualifications, and professional experience.



Clinica Family Health \& Wellness is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment based on race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, military status, or any other protected class under applicable federal, state, or local law.



Employees must meet applicable health and safety requirements, including an annual influenza (flu) vaccine, tuberculosis screening at hire, and any position specific requirements. Proof of required immunizations is required before employment begins. Exemptions and reasonable accommodations are considered.



Applications for this position will be accepted until the position is filled


Equal Opportunity Employer  

This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights (https://www.eeoc.gov/poster) notice from the Department of Labor.

jobs.description:
Behavioral Treatment Services provides accessible, integrated, and inclusive behavioral health services supporting clients throughout the criminal justice system.
  
  

Interested in mental health therapy? Looking to gain experience in addiction counseling?
  
  

Whether you are interested in therapy, treatment, behavioral health, psychology, social work, counseling, criminal justice, or restorative justice, we have a position for you!
  
  

Behavioral Treatment Services provides a continuum of specialized adult offender substance abuse and other treatment modalities. BTS is at the forefront of Colorado’s behavioral health and criminal justice programs and initiatives. BTS strives to provide a space toward client healing, reduce criminal recidivism, assist clients in working towards personal growth, and collaborate with the system and client to work towards mutually agreeable goals.
  
  

BTS provides clinical services, court related services, and specialized programs for adults involved in the criminal justice system. BTS provides services at community corrections sites (including residential treatment programs) and outpatient programs across Colorado.
  
  

In addition to this rewarding, meaningful, and exciting work, BTS offers:
  
  

* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) retirement plan with a generous 100% immediately vested employer match
* Paid life insurance
* Vacation, Sick, and Personal Paid Time Off
* 11 Paid Holidays per year
* A paid wellness hour 1x/week (within 40\-hour work week) to promote self\-care and wellness\-related activities
* Career pathing for continued growth and promotion from within
* Ongoing training such as Trauma\-Informed Care, First Aid Certification, Cultural Diversity, Professional Boundaries, Criminal Thinking, Motivational Interviewing
* Bi\-weekly individual and group licensure supervision (LCSW, LPC, CAC II/III/LAC) provided during work time at no cost to employee
* Flexibility on creating work schedule
* Paid CAC classes and attendance at CAC classes
* Incentives for covering extra shifts or groups
* BTS is a qualified employer for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program


**Title:** Peer Support Specialist
  
**Pay:** $21\.22/hr
  
**Location:** Lakewood \& Golden, CO
  
**Hours:** Part Time: Tues \- Thursday: 3pm\-7pm \& Friday: 8:30am\-2:30pm
  
  

OVERVIEW
  
  

Support clients by assisting them to succeed in the program through conducting client orientations,
  
  

facilitating sessions, and supporting the therapeutic milieu. Attends specialty courts to outreach and
  
  

recruit program participants.
  
  

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
  
  

* Support, promote and adhere to BTS’s mission, values and Code of Conduct.
* Reflect BTS’s commitment to treating all persons with dignity and respect.
* Maintain confidentiality of client and company information.
* Carry out all duties/responsibilities in accordance with Company values, policies and procedures, applicable laws and contractual obligations.
* Assist with initial program intake and orienting new clients.
* Participate in specialty court dockets, including outreach, planning client pro\-social events, client and court support, and client recruitment.
* Facilitate support groups, including but not limited to, initial orientation, continued care, peer run groups, individual support and care planning to assist clients in overcoming dependencies, developing pro\-social behavior or making other appropriate behavior or cognitive changes.
* Report clinical concerns and high\-risk persons and safety issues as they occur to other program staff and supervisor at staff report times. Follow clinical direction.
* Orders and picks up supplies/food for meetings as directed.
* Complete timely and accurate required documentation in all areas.
* Attend treatment team, clinical staffing and other required meetings.
* Drive personal car to court, jail and/or other sites as required, including in adverse weather.
* Attend required trainings and meetings, apply skills and knowledge.
* Regular and predictable attendance.
* Good steward of Company human, financial and capital resources.
* Participate effectively as a team member through communication, cooperation, information sharing and problem solving.
* Any other tasks or duties as assigned.


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
  
  

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE
  
  

* Personal lived experience with drug/alcohol abuse, criminal justice involvement and/or mental health problems with at least a minimum 1 year of current and sustained recovery.
* Must hold a valid CPFS/COPA credential in the state of Colorado


QUALIFICATIONS
  
  

* Computer skills \-\- Ability to enter data, generate reports and create communications from variety of software programs and databases, including EHRs.
* Ability to communicate effectively both verbally and in writing, and in either one\-on\-one or group settings.
* Ability to remain calm in and de\-escalate stressful situations.
* Ability to organize and manage time to complete work and meet deadlines.
* Detail focused/oriented.
* Knowledge of the cultural and socioeconomic characteristics and appropriate techniques and practices for the client population.
* Ability to interact effectively as a team member and independently with Company staff, stakeholders, and with diverse client base.
* Cannot be under current criminal justice supervision or have outstanding court cases, warrants, fees, etc.

-----------


The position is located within the Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System within the Community Engagement and Reintegration Service (CERS). The incumbent will be assigned to one of the facilities locations where a HUD\-VASH team is based. This position will be located at the Santa Maria VA Clinic.  

  



Learn more about this agency

jobs.title: Community Health Worker
jobs.description:
**About A.C.T.I.O.N.**



A.C.T.I.O.N. is a proposed community\-wide overdose prevention initiative that will expand access to FDA\-approved opioid overdose reversal medications (OORMs), community training, and treatment referral pathways across the twelve counties of Alabama's 4th Congressional District (Lauderdale, Colbert, Franklin, Marion, Lamar, Fayette, Walker, Winston, Cullman, Marshall, DeKalb, and Blount). This position is contingent upon receipt of federal SAMHSA grant funding.



**Position Summary**



The Community Health Worker (CHW) for Cluster 1 is responsible for opioid overdose reversal medication (OORM) distribution, overdose\-recognition and response training, and referral follow\-up within Marion, Lamar, and Fayette Counties, working in close partnership with the cluster's designated community partner organization. This locally embedded, field\-based role requires strong ties to the assigned counties.



**Key Responsibilities**



? Distribute FDA\-approved OORMs (naloxone and nalmefene) to bystanders, community sectors, and rural first responders within Marion, Lamar, and Fayette Counties.



? Deliver overdose\-recognition, response, and OORM\-administration training to both traditional partners (healthcare providers, pharmacies, EMS, school systems) and non\-traditional community sectors (e.g., gas station attendants, motel staff, retail employees, postal workers).



? Train local Training\-of\-Trainers cohorts to extend the training curriculum further into the community.



? Support referral and linkage follow\-up for individuals identified through prevention or overdose response activities, in coordination with the Program Coordinator/Data Lead.



? Maintain local relationships with the cluster's designated community partner, healthcare providers, pharmacies, faith\-based organizations, and schools.



? Complete required data collection instruments accurately and submit them to the Program Coordinator/Data Lead on the required schedule.



? Participate in the Local Community Prevention Collaborative and community\-facing outreach and distribution events.

**Minimum Qualifications**  

? Bachelor's degree in public health, social work, or a related field  

? Local, rural\-based residency or strong ties to Marion, Lamar, and Fayette Counties, with community trust and lived familiarity with the area.  

? Community health worker certification or equivalent lived or professional experience preferred.  

? Strong local community relationships and the trust of area residents.  

? Ability to complete Aletheia House's overdose\-recognition and naloxone\-administration training during onboarding (provided).  

? Reliable transportation and willingness to travel within the assigned counties for distribution and training visits.  

? Comfortable with basic data entry and reporting tools.


**Equal Opportunity Employer**  

Aletheia House is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status. Candidates are selected based on merit and qualifications only.


**Schedule**



Monday\-Friday 9:00am\-5:00pm; occasional weekends and evenings for community events

jobs.description:

**Overview**
------------



Otterbein is a not\-for\-profit, faith\-based ministry that is a national leader and innovator in retirement living communities and long\-term care. Otterbein is seeking a **Hospice RN,** to assist in the growth of our Hospice ministry. Otterbein Hospice compliments already strong independent senior services, outpatient capabilities and clinical facilities at Otterbein.



Hospice is a philosophy of care for those facing life\-limiting illnesses, as well as their families and caregivers. The focus of hospice care is to help patients experience peace, comfort, and quality of life while also offering support and services to their family and caregivers.



At Otterbein Hospice, our dedicated and compassionate team is here to help you through all stages of life's journey. When the time comes for hospice care, our team will involve you and your loved ones in your care options, and together with you, develop a personalized plan of care. Our team includes nurses, a chaplain and social worker for your care and support. We offer the peace that comes with being cared for in your home.

  


**If you're looking for an opportunity to serve in a mission\-focused ministry committed to transforming the model of elder care delivery this opportunity is for you.**


**Shift: Full\-Time 1st Shift, This is a traveling position covering: Batavia, Maineville, Loveland, Lebanon, and Springboro,**

Otterbein is seeking an enthusiastic and professional Hospice Nurse.


* This role is responsible for primary caseload.

* **Education**: Bachelor's degree in Nursing preferred. Graduate of approved nursing program

*\*Some benefits, including PTO and tuition reimbursement, are based on hours worked.*


**Why work for Otterbein SeniorLife:**



For more than 100 years, Otterbein has provided senior housing options rooted in respect and community. We're a non\-profit 501(c)(3\) health and human service organization, so our values and initiatives are focused on serving our residents.



Otterbein SeniorLife consists of lifestyle communities, revolutionary small house neighborhoods, home health, and hospice care in Ohio, Michigan and Indiana. We offer different lifestyle options for seniors through independent living, assisted living, skilled nursing, rehab, memory support, respite care, in\-home care, and hospice services.



Apply today and begin a meaningful career as a **Registered Nurse (RN) \- Case Manager** at Otterbein!

jobs.description:
Job Title: **Business \& Fulfillment Operations Program Coordinator**



Department: **Business \& Fulfillment Operations**



Reports to: **Senior Executive Director of Fulfillment Operations**

 **Overview \- About NoaNet**

  



NoaNet is a non\-profit mutual corporation providing wholesale telecommunications transport and is headquartered in the Spokane, Washington area. For over 20 years, it has operated a reliable public open\-access broadband communication network totaling over 3,300 fiber miles that provides rural areas access to broadband services, supporting last\-mile providers that serve more than 260,000 customers.  **About Everyone On**


Everyone On envisions a society where every individual has equal access to technology, expanding their potential and creating a more connected and thriving world. We design high\-impact, community\-centered programs replicated nationwide through strategic partnerships with government, corporations and nonprofits.


Our holistic approach to digital inclusion focuses on connecting under\-resourced individuals to affordable internet and computers, providing digital skills training to individuals and organizations, and advancing fair and just policies. jobs.description:
Company Overview:
**Work Where it Matters**

  

Akima Global Logistics (AGL), an Akima company, is not just another operations contractor. As an Alaska Native Corporation (ANC), our mission and purpose extend beyond our exciting federal projects as we support our shareholder communities in Alaska.

  

At AGL, the work you do every day makes a difference in the lives of our 15,000 Iñupiat shareholders, a group of Alaska natives from one of the most remote and harshest environments in the United States.

 **For our shareholders,** AGL provides support and employment opportunities and contributes to the survival of a culture that has thrived above the Arctic Circle for more than 10,000 years.

 **For our government customers,** AGL delivers comprehensive supply, transportation, and maintenance services designed to optimize and maintain operations.

 **As an AGL employee,** you will be surrounded by a challenging, yet supportive work environment that is committed to innovation and diversity, two of our most important values. You will also have access to our comprehensive benefits and competitive pay in addition to growth opportunities and excellent retirement options.


Description:

Assesses psychological health using current American Psychological Association Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, develops treatment plans, and modifies plans over time in response to patient progress. Documents assessments and treatments. Consults with health and psychology professionals, helps develop and put treatment plans in place.


Responsibilities:
* Behavioral Health Specialist will serve as a member of the Behavioral Health team in support of the Texas Military Department. Providing service members comprehensive clinical screening, assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning, resource referral and connection, crisis intervention, risk/safety assessment, critical incident counseling, behavioral health profile initiation and tracking, behavioral health psychoeducation, SRP/JRSOI support, Command guidance and recommendation.
* The position engages in routine contact with Service Members, their leadership, and treatment providers to ensure all behavioral health needs are met through careful and collaborative assessment.
* Responsible for record\-keeping; expected to maintain detailed records regarding their clients’ treatment plans and progress using a provided electronic health record.
* Completes a thorough intake evaluation of each client’s mental and physical state and their needs upon presenting for treatment. In some cases, the Behavioral Health Specialist may also need to consult with the client’s military leadership during intake and while developing a treatment plan.
* Provide ongoing clinical case management, outreach, and regularly make fitness for duty decisions in consultation with a team of licensed providers.
* Perform in a remote setting with an anticipated 25% travel requirement within the State of Texas.


Qualifications:
* A minimum of a Master’s degree in social work.
* Active Texas LCSW Certification.
* Experience and direct contact with patients.
* Strong working knowledge of human behavioral theory and application of theory to practice.
* Excellent communication skills.
* High level of professionalism.
* Organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Capable of simultaneously working in multiple computer applications (Microsoft Office, TEAMS, electronic health records, and others).
* Ability to work under pressure and in mental health crisis situations.
* Rounded understanding of behavioral health conditions and treatments.
* Ability to pass a pre\-employment background check.
* Ability to receive a favorable TIER\-1 investigation result and obtain/maintain a Common Access Card (CAC).
* U.S. citizen with a valid driver license.
* Experience working with military personnel and/or in a military setting.
* Familiarity with National Guard Bureau behavioral health policy and regulation.
* Independent remote work environment.
* Interdisciplinary experience working with leaders in large organizations.
* Comfort presenting on topics of behavioral and mental health to large groups.
* Knowledge of military and military family life culture.
* Use of evidence\-based screening tools (PHQ\-9, GAD\-7, PCL\-5, CSSRS, DAST\-10, AUDIT\-C).

**Pay \& Benefits:**

* Salary: GS\-12, Step 1 (Austin, TX locality pay rate).

We provide Senior Living and Assisted Living apartment homes for adults 62 years of age and older (and people with qualifying mobility impairment disabilities). Our nonprofit organization is currently seeking a **Full\-Time Assisted Living Care Coordinator** to join our team! A compassionate, skilled Care Coordinator to support the behavioral health and emotional well\-being of older adults. Learn more about this agency

-----------------------

U.S. Citizens, Nationals or those who owe allegiance to the U.S.

Current federal employees of the hiring agency that posted the job announcement.

----------


  

**VA Careers \- Social Work**: https://youtube.com/embed/enRhz\_ua\_UU

The incumbent is an unlicensed entry level Social Worker assigned to the Housing and Urban Development Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (HUD\-VASH). Under the supervision of a licensed clinician, the Social Worker duties include working with a multidisciplinary team and interacting with Veterans, family members, significant others, community agencies, VA, and non\-VA healthcare providers in addressing Veteran homelessness.

----------------

* your performance and conduct;
* the needs and interests of the agency;

Upon completion of your trial period, your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest.
### **Qualifications**

**Basic Requirements**:

**Overview**
------------



Otterbein is a not\-for\-profit, faith\-based ministry that is a national leader and innovator in retirement living communities and long\-term care. Otterbein is seeking a **Hospice RN,** to assist in the growth of our Hospice ministry. Otterbein Hospice compliments already strong independent senior services, outpatient capabilities and clinical facilities at Otterbein.



Hospice is a philosophy of care for those facing life\-limiting illnesses, as well as their families and caregivers. The focus of hospice care is to help patients experience peace, comfort, and quality of life while also offering support and services to their family and caregivers.



At Otterbein Hospice, our dedicated and compassionate team is here to help you through all stages of life's journey. When the time comes for hospice care, our team will involve you and your loved ones in your care options, and together with you, develop a personalized plan of care. Our team includes nurses, a chaplain and social worker for your care and support. We offer the peace that comes with being cared for in your home.

  


**If you're looking for an opportunity to serve in a mission\-focused ministry committed to transforming the model of elder care delivery this opportunity is for you.**
